weather_line: Autumn fully committed · hats unexplained · hollows receptive

stories.headline: Third Duck Arrives; Hat Identified; Pemwick Goes Very Still for a Long Moment
body: A third charmed rubber duck appeared on the Jeep overnight, bringing the total to three and the official inquiry to what junior analyst Pemwick has formally logged as 'a significant development, possibly.' The new duck wears a flat cap — dark wool, expertly felted — and Pemwick has confirmed that all three hats share not only the same stitch count but the same underlying pattern: a six-point crown construction not documented in any Ministry catalogue of enchanted haberdashery currently on record.

The flat cap, the wide-brim amber felt, and the original undocumented hat form, according to Pemwick's quietly excited three-page memo, a complete set. He has cross-referenced the pattern against seven regional databases and one obscure appendix in the 1987 Wizarding Craft Guild registry, where the entry reads only: 'Six-Crown Travelling Hat, maker known, location variable, leaves no trace, always returns.' The name associated with the entry has been redacted. Someone redacted it a long time ago, apparently on purpose.

The Duck Provenance Office has upgraded the inquiry to Priority Amber and requested access to the Guild's original registration files. The Guild has replied that it will consider the request. Pemwick has circled the word 'consider' three times and pinned the letter to his board. The Jeep, for its part, now has three very well-dressed ducks on its bonnet and appears entirely satisfied with the arrangement.

stories.headline: Saturday's Outstanding File Cleared Before the Ink Dried; Goblins Log the Time and Say Nothing, Which Is How They Say Everything
body: One outstanding account dispute remained on the Friday ledger when business closed — a billing discrepancy across three vaults, two currencies, and an argument about the conversion rate for a coin denomination that ceased to be legal tender in 1934. It had been escalating quietly for eleven days.

Christine reviewed it over her morning tea. By the time the tea was finished, the file was annotated, resolved, and returned to the clerk's desk with a note that included, in the margin, the correct 1934 conversion rate sourced from memory. The Gringotts Senior Council logged the timestamp and filed it without comment. In goblin record-keeping, a timestamp filed without comment is the equivalent of a standing ovation. The weekend is now clear.

stories.headline: Saturday Opens Well; Steve Locates a Thing He Has Been Looking For Since April; the Jeep Receives No Further Ducks but Is Clearly Ready
body: Saturday morning conditions were reported as favourable across the household. Steve located, behind a lower shelf in the garage, the specific bracket he has been searching for since April. It is in good condition. The enchanted Jeep, freshly attended to and now presiding over three well-hatted ducks, was observed facing the direction of the Gorge with what one neighbour described as 'intent.' No expedition has been formally announced but the Jeep does not appear to require one.
The biscuit tin has been returned to the counter for the fifth consecutive day — a household record. Analysts confirm the position is stable. The tin has not commented.

stories.headline: Guild Registry Appendix Entry Found Redacted; Nobody Remembers Who Did It; The Handwriting, Notably, Is Excellent
body: Archivists at the Wizarding Craft Guild have confirmed that the 1987 appendix entry for 'Six-Crown Travelling Hat' was redacted by hand, in a very fine ink, using a nib described by the current senior archivist as 'frankly enviable.' The redactor's identity is not recorded. The Guild has no policy on self-redaction, because until today no one had thought to write one.

Pemwick has requested a copy of the original handwriting for comparative analysis. The Guild archivist has said she will look into it. She was observed, after the call ended, looking not into the files but out of the window, with an expression that the Ministry duty clerk described as 'like someone who knows something and has decided the knowing is enough for now.'

familiars_corner: Lucy: The biscuit tin is on the counter. It has been on the counter for five days. Lucy has not touched it. She would like everyone to note that she has not touched it. She is establishing something.
Ellie: A third duck has appeared on the Jeep. Ellie investigated it this morning, found it wearing a hat, and concluded that the hat was for her. It was not for her. She remains confident.
Jersey: Saturday. Lap available. Lap located. Jersey's work for the day is complete and he has filed his report from a horizontal position.
founding_editor_note: Six-point crown construction is sound work — that's a proper join at the apex. Whoever's making those hats knows what they're doing. I'd have used a slightly heavier wool, but I'm not saying it's wrong. — D.

in_brief.sport: Weekend Lifting Correspondent notes that Christine's Saturday conditioning has been logged, completed, and is none of the goblins' business.
in_brief.forecast: Hollows: atmospheric and receptive. Ridgeline: quietly expectant. Hat weather across all elevations. The Gorge will be ready when you are.

storyline_updates.title: The Duck Bandit Returns
storyline_updates.summary: Day 3: A third duck has appeared, completing a set of three hats (original undocumented style, wide-brim amber felt, flat wool cap) all using a six-point crown construction. Pemwick has traced the pattern to a redacted 1987 Craft Guild appendix entry — 'Six-Crown Travelling Hat, maker known, location variable, leaves no trace, always returns' — with the maker's name removed in excellent handwriting. The Guild has received a request for the original files and is 'considering' it. The Guild archivist's demeanour suggests she knows more than she is saying. Priority Amber. Day 4 should bring a breakthrough: either the Guild archivist provides a partial clue (initials, a location, a phrase), or someone in the broader Jeep community — perhaps another recipient of well-hatted ducks — comes forward and recognises the style from a previous encounter years ago, giving the Bandit a shape, a history, and perhaps a motive that points warmly toward Christine and Steve specifically.
